cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's Audit Machine test the equipment and leases of HANGS Construction Services.
It agrees the equipment register to the books.
Then it rolls the register forward, asset by asset.
Now it checks every purchase against its invoice, line by line.
A repair of about $41,000 was booked as equipment.
One purchase had no signed approval.
A crane sold in March is still on the books.
Depreciation spreads cost over an asset's life. One excavator's life is half the policy's.
Then it reads every rental. Under the lease rules, a long rental goes on the balance sheet as a debt.
One crane rental is really a lease, a debt missing from the books.
Now it adds up what it found and sets it against materiality.
Then it writes the workpapers and a draft findings memo for the CPA.

All done. In profit, the errors nearly cancel out. But over $2.1 million of lease debt is missing from the balance sheet, and the sold crane is still on the books. Ten items stay open. The CPA, a person, concludes and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
